title: Two- and three-body bound states in one-dimensional Fermi bipolaron with three-body interaction
abstract: We discuss the ground-state properties of two bosonic (or spin-1/2 fermionic in a singlet spin state) impurities immersed in a one-dimensional ideal Fermi gas with only the three-body contact interaction accounted for. Despite its simplicity, the considered model is found to demonstrate a variety of medium-induced few-body bound states. Particularly, using variational calculations with trial wave functions that correctly take into account one particle-hole excitation, we predict the emergence of a dimer state and several trimer states over a wide range of the three-body coupling parameter.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the formation of bound states—specifically dimers and trimers—when two impurities are placed in a 1D Fermi gas interacting via a three-body contact potential. Using variational methods, the authors predict that multiple stable few-body complexes emerge across various coupling strengths, demonstrating rich medium-induced physics.
main_problem: The study investigates the ground-state properties of two impurities immersed in a one-dimensional ideal Fermi gas, specifically focusing on medium-induced few-body bound states.
main_result: Variational calculations predict the emergence of both dimer and several trimer bound states over a wide range of the three-body coupling parameter. The dimer state is generally found to be energetically preferable.
method: The analysis employs variational calculations using trial wave functions that incorporate up to one particle-hole excitation, solving resulting coupled integral equations.
model_or_system: The system models two bosonic (or spin-1/2 fermionic) impurities interacting via a three-body contact interaction within a 1D ideal Fermi gas host. The physics is captured by an effective Hamiltonian describing the center-of-mass motion of the impurities.
key_observables: Energies of the bound states ($\epsilon_{	ext{dimer}}$ and $\epsilon_{	ext{trimer}}$), which are compared against T-matrix results.
important_parameters: The three-body coupling constant ($g_{3,\Lambda}$), the Fermi energy ($\epsilon_F$), and the mass ratio of impurities to host fermions ($m/m_I$).
main_assumptions: The model assumes only a zero-range, three-body interaction is present. The variational ansatz includes up to one particle-hole excitation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares calculated dimer and trimer energies across various mass ratios and coupling parameters against T-matrix results. Figure 2 identifies multiple branches of trimer states ($\epsilon_{	ext{trimer}, n}$) relative to the vacuum branch.
paper_structure: The paper derives an effective Hamiltonian for the impurities interacting with the host, then applies variational methods to determine the ground state energies for both dimer and trimer configurations by solving coupled integral equations.
why_interesting: This work explores how non-standard interactions (three-body) can induce complex few-body correlations in low-dimensional quantum gases, providing insights into emergent many-body physics beyond simple two-body scattering.
